title: Over a field, few differentials at a point imply smoothness there
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\Omega_{S/k}$ be the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. If $$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)\le\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S),$$ then $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]: there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $S_g$ is a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

proof.text: Use the geometric closed-point differential-fibre comparison to obtain K, a maximal prime qK over q, and the equality of the two differential-fibre finranks. This does not use the dimension-bound hypothesis or assume smoothness.

The tensor commutation K tensor_k S ≃ S tensor_k K induces a homeomorphism of prime spectra. Point dimension is invariant under this homeomorphism: pull back each open neighborhood and use the homeomorphism of the neighborhood subspaces in both directions. Field-extension invariance, applied on the S-first tensor product, and the contraction equality then give dim_q Spec S = dim_qK Spec (K tensor_k S).

Finite type survives tensor base change. Apply the closed-point dimension lemma at the maximal prime qK to identify its point dimension with ringKrullDim of the localization. Together with the fibre finrank equality, rewrite the assumed inequality to the local-ring dimension bound required by the algebraically closed maximal-ideal criterion. That criterion gives a smooth principal localization away from qK, hence IsSmoothAtPrime K qK.
Apply field-extension smoothness descent at qK, then rewrite its contraction to q.
